headline: Leverage rebuilt in a day: funding back to 10.61% from 3.52%, Coinbase premium at the 1.3rd percentile, spot still absent before FOMC.
summary: Last issue's "leverage flushed" call was refuted within a day: weighted funding is back at 10.61%, rising on all three venues, while the Coinbase premium fell to −0.177%. Price holds 0.65% above the true market mean of 79,484 on perp longs, not spot. Bull day 18, no exit trigger; watch FOMC at 02:00 Oct 29 Taipei (18:00 UTC Oct 28) and the Oct 30 monthly expiry.

findings.title: Leverage rebuilt in a day while the spot premium sank to a record low zone
findings.lean_why: Leveraged longs without spot support are short-term downside fuel; with price hugging the true market mean, a break could trigger cascading liquidations.
findings.what: Oct 26 weighted funding 10.61% (last issue 3.52%), with perps 2.5 points above the futures basis median of 5.68% (last issue 3.64 below); the same day the Coinbase premium was −0.177%, the 1.3rd percentile of the site's 299-day record, 7-day average −0.13%; the close of 80,002 is only 0.65% above the true market mean of 79,484 (bitcoin-data Oct 20), a level signal now 5 days running.
findings.why: Decomposing derivatives first: the rebound was not one venue; Hyperliquid 1.04% → 10.95%, OKX 7.64% → 10.95%, Deribit 1.85% → 8.18% moved together, and the 30-day risk reversal narrowed from −4.90 to −3.72, so options also shed downside protection; both derivative types agree. Spot says the opposite: the Coinbase premium is in the site's low zone, ETFs lost ~$773M over Oct 22–23 (The Block), and stablecoin supply fell 0.77% over 7 days (DefiLlama). External check: Glassnode's Market Pulse Week 44 (Oct 26) says leverage did not clear with the drop, with long funding payments above the high band and spot CVD at −$80.5M. Derivatives turning up while spot weakens is a contradiction, and the contradiction is the finding.
findings.alt: Hyperliquid settles hourly and OKX every 8 hours, so single snapshots are noisy and last issue's 3.52% may have been the outlier; 10.6% annualized is not high for a bull phase. The Coinbase premium compares USD with USDT, so USDT's own premium or discount can bias it; the site's premium record covers only 299 days.
findings.history: The brief has no historical sample for this "funding rebound + spot premium in the low zone" combination, so it is background only; the most recent similar setup was Oct 21–22, followed by $773M of ETF outflows over two days and a long flush.
findings.so: Last issue's "leverage flushed, less liquidation fuel" call is refuted, and cascade risk on a break of 79,484 is back; but this is short-term structure: the market stage (bull day 18) and the exit framework are unchanged, and the nearest framework action point remains the 200-day MA 8.8% below.
findings.next: By Oct 30 (FOMC and monthly expiry): a daily Coinbase premium back above 0 would mean spot is catching up and the contradiction resolves; a close below 78,000 (the monthly max pain, below the 79,000 bid wall) would confirm leveraged longs turning into downside fuel.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 44
items.points: After a failed push to 85K, BTC is back near 80K; futures OI $37.5B (+2.7%), long funding payments above the high band; perp CVD −$288M, spot CVD −$80.5M; 25Δ skew 10.4% (prior 8.9%); weekly ETF net inflow $296.8M but front-loaded; ETF MVRV 1.4, below its low band; supply in profit 67.3%. Conclusion: weak and defensive, not a structural break.
items.meaning: "Leverage not cleared, spot stepped back" matches today's finding; its skew widening uses a different tenor, while the site's 30-day risk reversal narrowed to −3.72 today; the two are not compared, and the site keeps its own series.

items.title: Quantifying Support and Resistance: Proximity-Weighted CBD
items.points: Weights the cost-basis distribution by distance from spot; when PSI (weighted share of supply below spot) rises above 50%, support dominates; in Apr–May 2026 an 83.6K–85.4K resistance band formed before price fell to the low 60Ks; related October posts treat 85K–87.5K as resistance and ~80K as support.
items.meaning: A methodology study that can be compared with the site's ±5% supply concentration of 13.19% and the URPD clusters at 82–86K above price; the site does not adopt its thresholds.

items.title: Perpetual Preferred Stock: The Newest Demand Catalyst for Bitcoin
items.points: Perpetual preferreds have funded 135,979 BTC of corporate buying since 2025-07 (to Oct 5, over 0.5% of supply), more than 95,000 BTC in March–May alone with over $7B raised; it works only while BTC's gains exceed the dividend cost.
items.meaning: Strategy buying back STRC instead of bitcoin last week confirms this demand channel is slowing; consistent with the spot absence in the site's Coinbase premium, and not used for the cycle call.
